status: pilot: 10 of ~24 aquarium plants, first pass, unverified

items.name: Anubias (Anubias barteri / nana)

sources.label: Very easy
sources.why: tolerates very low to strong light, no CO2, slow growth

sources.label: Easy (details table: very easy); light demand Low
sources.why: no CO2 needed, low to strong light

sources.label: Beginner
sources.why: low light, no CO2, low nutrient demand; keep rhizome on wood/stone

items.reason: Three sources agree: very forgiving, slow, low light; only rule is do not bury the rhizome.

items.name: Amazon sword (Echinodorus)

sources.label: Care Level: Easy
sources.why: heavy root feeder: needs 3 in substrate, root tabs every 1-2 months, iron; melt after planting

sources.label: Beginner
sources.why: low light listed, no CO2, high nutrient demand (root tabs), needs big space
calls swords easy; moderate light, root tabs, cichlids may damage; some hybrids need more care

items.reason: All three say easy; the only demand is root feeding (tabs) and room to grow.

items.name: Rotala (Rotala rotundifolia / red stem types)

sources.label: Beginner (base form, high maintenance); H'ra and Blood Red intermediate
sources.why: moderate light, CO2 optional; fast growth needs trimming; red/H'ra forms need high light + CO2

sources.label: Beginner-friendly
sources.why: medium-high light, no CO2 needed; red colour from high light; iron, algae on leaves

items.reason: Plain R. rotundifolia is easy; deep red or H'ra forms are level 2 (high light + CO2). Only two pages opened (Petco 403).

items.name: Carpet plant (dwarf baby tears / Monte Carlo style)

sources.label: Advanced
sources.why: very high light (80+ PAR) plus pressurized CO2 plus rich substrate together; missing one gives recession and algae

sources.label: Medium
sources.why: stable water, bright light, CO2 strongly recommended; leggy without; melt on planting

sources.label: Moderate and slow
sources.why: possible without CO2 but 3-4 months, needs aquasoil, dry start, trimming; algae

items.reason: Labels split 3/2/2 but all reasons need strong light + CO2 + rich substrate for HC; Monte Carlo is easier (closer to 2). Flip Aquatics 429, Petco/2Hr Aquarist 403.

items.name: Java moss

sources.label: Very easy
sources.why: low to high light, no CO2; any snippet regrows (nuisance)

sources.label: Easy (table: very easy)
sources.why: low light OK, no CO2; needs trimming; spindly in low light

sources.label: Very Easy
sources.why: algae/detritus on moss if too much light or poor flow

items.reason: Three sources agree; main chore is trimming and keeping debris/algae off.

items.name: Dwarf hairgrass (Eleocharis)

sources.label: Moderate
sources.why: medium-high light, CO2 strongly recommended, heavy root feeder; algae if light without CO2

sources.label: Moderate
sources.why: medium-high light, 20-30 ppm CO2 advised, slow (3-6 months) without; trimming; algae

items.reason: Two sources agree and none disagree: carpets reliably only with strong light, CO2 and rich substrate; slow without.

items.name: Amazon frogbit (floating)

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: medium to high light, CO2 not needed; dense mats shade the tank

sources.label: Beginner (FAQ: sits somewhere in the middle)
sources.why: leaves rot with surface agitation/wet leaves; fast growth needs thinning; shades others

items.reason: Easy to grow; the real work is calm surface, thinning and keeping leaves dry; Guidarium hedges toward middle.

items.name: Cryptocoryne (wendtii / parva)

sources.label: Very easy
sources.why: low-medium light, CO2 optional; crypt melt after changes; root tabs in gravel
beginner-friendly but notorious for melt; recovers
relatively easy but sensitive to change; emersed-grown leaves melt; consistency matters

sources.label: Easy to moderate
sources.why: needs more light (40-100 PAR), very slow, active soil or root tabs

items.reason: Wendtii clearly beginner; parva is slower and fussier (borderline 2). Main risk is melt after changes, which usually recovers.

items.name: Red stem plant (Ludwigia / Alternanthera / Rotala red)

sources.label: Easy (repens, palustris); easy to moderate (Super Red, Rubin); moderate (arcuata)
sources.why: red needs 40+ PAR light, regular iron dosing, moderate nitrate; CO2 for the redder cultivars

sources.label: Easy
sources.why: no CO2 needed; red colour needs 0.5 W/L plus, low nitrate, good iron

sources.label: Medium
sources.why: high light essential for colour and to stop lower leaf drop; CO2 beneficial; iron/potassium

items.reason: Staying alive is easy (1) but a good red look needs bright light, iron and nitrate tuning (2); plain green-red Ludwigia repens is easier, reineckii and Super Red harder.

items.name: Pothos (riparium / hanging on the tank)

sources.label: Beginner
sources.why: low light, no CO2; leaves must stay out of water; trim fast growth; needs room
easy to grow; keep leaves above water; toxic to pets; roots overgrow and can starve other plants; submerged growth poor

items.reason: Easy as long as only roots are wet and leaves stay dry; two sources, no disagreement but both hobby/retail sites.
